comments.value:
A world-level database would be great and many would not mind paying for the extra server processing. There could even be a Creator Economy incentive, where if VRChat is earning enough revenue from your world, it automatically qualifies for that database without having to pay for it, helping avoid the issue of if a creator has to stop paying into it for some reason causing the world to break.

Though handling syncing between multiple instances for the example you give sounds a little iffy. What happens when a different user in two instances both move the box at the same time? Would have to transmit a TakeOwnership signal to the global, and return false if it's already in ownership, or otherwise have it transmit that to all other instances. Not allowing you to pick it up until you get that response to avoid race-condition situations.

details:
I need something like a "WorldData" storage object that would let me sync changes to a world between all users who visit and modify the world. 

The simplest use case for this is something like a world with a box that can be moved by players. If someone comes into the world and moves the box, I want a way for the next user who visits the world to see the box at the location that it was moved to (with the corresponding rotation). 

Since VRCurl URLs cannot be generated at runtime, and PlayerData is tied to individual user accounts, I'm finding it exceptionally difficult to implement experiences like these. I ultimately need to pre-generate thousands of urls in order to be able to transmit all of the possible positions and rotations for all objects in the scene that can be moved, making certain experiences prohibitively difficult (or impossible) to implement.

A simple data storage object like PlayerData but for the world itself would solve this problem elegantly, and open up a huge range of new and interesting experiences within VRChat. I would be willing to pay a subscription/fee per-world for this kind of storage, and I imagine that others would be as well. It would be an absolute game changer and feels like something that the community has been yearning for for a long time.
title: Add world-level persistent data storage
